name: BESTIA
description: Bestia (The Beast) is a classic Italian gambling card game of the Rams family, dating back to the 18th century. It combines standard trick-taking mechanics with a high-stakes pool-betting system. Players win shares of the pot by taking tricks, but failing to win a single trick results in the 'Bestia' penalty: the player must match the entire current pot for the next round. It is a game of high tension, calculation, and bluffing, especially popular during festive seasons in Italy.

content.text: Bestia (The Beast) is a classic Italian gambling card game of the Rams family, dating back to the 18th century. It combines standard trick-taking mechanics with a high-stakes pool-betting system. Players win shares of the pot by taking tricks, but failing to win a single trick results in the 'Bestia' penalty: the player must match the entire current pot for the next round. It is a game of high tension, calculation, and bluffing, especially popular during festive seasons in Italy.

Derived from the French game 'La Bête' (The Beast) and related to the English 'Loo'. It became extremely popular in 18th and 19th-century Italy, evolving from 'Lest' or 'Bête' which spread across European courts.
4 to 6 players; 5 is considered the ideal number for balanced play.

A standard 40-card Italian deck (Swords, Batons, Cups, Coins). With Latin suits, ranks from high to low are: Ace, 3, King (Re), Horse (Cavallo), Jack (Fante), 7, 6, 5, 4, 2. When French suits are used, the Queen replaces the Horse.
Chips or currency for the central pot.
Deal 3 cards to each player (usually clockwise). One card is turned face up to determine the Trump suit.

items.text: Five-Card Bestia: Each player receives 5 cards and 5 tricks are played; the pot is divided into five shares.
Briscola Bestia: Uses the point-values and ranking system of Briscola (Ace=11, 3=10, King=4...) rather than simple trick counts.
